clue.text: Sudden work by a photographer

definitions.meaning: a ... decision or ... election is one made suddenly, without warning
a quick photograph taken with a camera is a snapshot, shortened

explanation.surface: A photographer produces a picture in a flash.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an adjective for something abrupt and a noun for a quick photograph.

clue.text: Determination that's needed to control an estate

definitions.text: that's needed to control an estate
definitions.meaning: a testament directs how a dead person's property is handled

explanation.surface: Running a country estate takes grit and resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is one sense; the legal document directing the disposal of a dead person's estate is the other.

clue.text: Luxury car kept in warmer climes

indicators.note: the answer is kept inside the run of letters of the words warmer climes

explanation.surface: A posh motor is garaged somewhere sunny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' signals letters held inside warMER Climes.
explanation.definitionFit: Short informal name for a Mercedes, a luxury German make of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Overlook fellow blocking traffic marker

indicators.note: the fellow stands in the way inside the marker, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a cone is the plastic marker put on roads
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Someone ignores a man standing in the way of a road cone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' is a college don, a common crossword sense; 'blocking' has him standing inside the marker.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgive or let pass an offence is to overlook it, a close synonym.

clue.text: How an all-round athlete competes whatever happens

definitions.meaning: a versatile athlete would enter in whichever event

explanation.surface: A decathlete-type athlete will take part regardless of circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning regardless, and read literally it describes an athlete entering every discipline.

clue.text: Source of power in Rome gone, displaced

indicators.note: the letters of in Rome gone are moved out of their places into a new order

explanation.surface: Power has left Rome, which is in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced' rearranges INROMEGONE.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the compartment housing the motors is where its propulsion comes from.

clue.text: Attractive element that's good in French painter is linked to medium

indicators.note: good's letter goes inside the painter's name

parts.note: Edouard Manet, French painter
M is the size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A charming feature of a fine French painter is tied to his medium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' suggests paint; here it is M, as on clothing sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: The force pulling iron to a magnet, or personal allure, is an attracting quality.

clue.text: Reportedly useless means for gauging wind

indicators.note: as it is reported, i.e. spoken, the word sounds like another

parts.note: vain means futile, useless

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a wind-measuring device is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: A weathervane turns to show which way the wind blows.

clue.text: Left in election following excellent change of direction

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the word for an election

parts.note: a vote is a ballot or election
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A politician switches policy after an excellent election result for the Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a link word but gives F.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of opinion or policy is an about-turn, a change of direction.

clue.text: Law operative given a lead?

parts.note: a police officer given a lead sounds like a detective getting a clue, but this operative is walked on a leash

explanation.surface: A detective receives a tip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' reads as a clue in an investigation; really it is the strap a handler holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained canine working for the police is kept on a leash, a lead.

clue.text: Lodge out of the South presumably

parts.note: whoever is out of the South is presumably up in the North, giving IN plus N for north
whoever is out of the South is presumably up in the North, giving IN plus N for north

explanation.surface: A lodge, it would seem, is not in the South.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a whimsical inference: not in the South, so IN N(orth).
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small hotel or hostelry offering rooms for travellers.

clue.text: Online reference for short golf course

indicators.note: the word for the golf course is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: links is a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: A web pointer leads to a nine-hole golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of LINKS; links is a coastal golf course, as at St Andrews.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyperlink on a web page refers the reader elsewhere online.

clue.text: Fool that may be picked, critically

definitions.meaning: ...-picking is petty fault-finding, so the louse egg is what a critic picks

explanation.surface: A critic chooses an idiot to pick on.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person in British slang, and the louse egg of nit-picking, the pedantic criticising habit.

clue.text: Utter it, for instance, going to church

parts.note: the word it is an example of a pronoun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone says something on the way to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a word here, not a reference back; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To say a word aloud or articulate it is to utter it.

clue.text: GB capital's altered former supermarket giveaway

indicators.note: the letters of GB capital's are altered into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the 's is read as a plain S, giving CAPITALS

explanation.surface: London has changed, a relic of shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges GBCAPITALS; British shops once handed out free carrier bags before charges came in.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops used to hand out thin polythene carriers free until a levy ended the practice.

clue.text: Old drink holder in another, clearly empty — sign of hotel guests?

indicators.note: one container sits inside the other

parts.note: a can is another drink holder
a cup holds a drink

indicators.note: clearly emptied of its inside leaves only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An old cup inside a can, plainly vacant, hints at hotel guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts one drink holder inside 'another'; 'empty' removes the middle of 'clearly', leaving its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms taken show a hotel is being used; the occupancy rate measures guests staying.

clue.text: Six deliveries — company put in too many

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled
a crowd is a company of people

explanation.surface: A cricket team's six balls are watched by too many spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER in cricket is a set of six balls from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack too many people into a space is to cram it beyond capacity.

clue.text: One-time premier artiste denies embraces

indicators.note: the phrase artiste denies holds the name inside its letters

explanation.surface: A performer refuses a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' signals letters inside artistE DENies; Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister 1955-57.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was a British prime minister in the 1950s, a former premier.

clue.text: Learner following cheats at work — traditional schoolboy resource?

indicators.note: the learner's letter comes after the rest
the letters of cheats are set to work, rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A pupil follows cheats at their homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' signals the anagram, and 'following' places the learner's letter last; 'cheats' looks like the subject but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather shoulder bag was the classic way schoolboys carried books.

clue.text: Period recalled in very new part of mosque

indicators.note: the reversed period goes inside the word for very new

parts.note: mint condition means brand new

indicators.note: called back, so the word for period is read in reverse

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A time in history is remembered inside a newly built mosque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' means called back, turning the period round; 'in' then places it within 'very new', as in mint condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Small measurement seen to be faulty? It's huge

parts.note: one millimetre, 1 mm, with the 1 written as Roman I

indicators.note: the letters of seen are faulty, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiny reading is found to be wrong; actually it is enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small measurement' is 1mm, giving IMM; 'to be faulty' rearranges SEEN into ENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means vast, of enormous size, an exact synonym of huge.

clue.text: Prevent bowls rolling backwards

indicators.note: the word for bowls rolls back, read from its end

parts.note: pots are bowls or vessels

explanation.surface: Bowls players halt a wood rolling the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowls' suggests the lawn game; it means pots.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or block something is to keep it from happening.

clue.text: A parliamentarian's sent in to court part of French board

indicators.note: the parliamentarian is sent inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a member of parliament

explanation.surface: A French MP is dispatched to court, part of a board.
explanation.walkthrough: The French board is a cheeseboard, not a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft Normandy cheese would appear on a French cheeseboard.

clue.text: Pub to exclude lawyers

definitions.meaning: to ... someone is to ban them

explanation.surface: Lawyers are banned from a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one short word: a drinking place, to ban, and the barristers' profession.

clue.text: Pressure to avoid item in broadcast

indicators.note: the word for item avoids the pressure letter, which is left out

parts.note: an item is a couple, a pair
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Pressure to keep a story off the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'item' is a couple, as in 'they're an item'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on radio or television is to broadcast, as in airing a show.

clue.text: Figure of veneration in entertaining company

indicators.note: the word in hosts, holds within it, the company abbreviation

explanation.surface: A revered figure is good company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' means holding as a host does, so the word 'in' wraps round the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A holy image venerated in Orthodox churches, or more generally an idolised figure.

clue.text: Very welcoming dame prone to get excited

indicators.note: the letters of dame prone are excited, stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An older lady is prone to over-excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get excited' rearranges DAMEPRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Greeting someone with arms spread wide shows a warm, effusive welcome.

clue.text: Nothing in cash machine? Not big matter

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the cash machine's abbreviation

parts.note: an ATM is an automated teller machine
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An empty cashpoint is no big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not big matter' reads as 'no big deal' but defines a tiny particle of matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest unit of a chemical element is a minuscule piece of matter.

clue.text: Dinner, maybe, from tin, say, that's timeless

indicators.note: without time, so the time abbreviation is removed

parts.note: tin is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: Dinner from a can, eternally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' removes T, the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is one example of a repast eaten at a set time of day.

clue.text: Day in court?

definitions.meaning: a calendar day, such as the fourth of July
to court someone is to woo them, go out romantically

explanation.surface: A trial day in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar day and a romantic outing or wooing; 'court' misleads toward law.

clue.text: Cautious manner restrains king

indicators.note: the word for manner holds the king within it

parts.note: a way is a manner of doing something
R is Rex, king

explanation.surface: A careful style keeps the monarch in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restrains' puts R inside WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on guard against danger, careful and watchful.

clue.text: Lady toils busily around yard changing sides?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the yard abbreviation
the letters of lady toils bustle about into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman works hard about the garden, switching teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busily' rearranges LADYTOILS into DISLOALTY; 'around' puts Y inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfaithfulness, as when someone defects to the other camp, betraying their allegiance.
